title: Empirical Latency-Cost Tradeoff Lab & Runbook
creator: Lena Cho
description: Run a portable, repeatable lab to quantify latency vs unit-cost tradeoffs across model variants, quantization levels, and routing policies. Produce a practical runbook teams can use when selecting models and deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) for production use cases that are sensitive to both latency and cost.
background: We frequently get questions from platform and product teams about whether to accept modest latency increases to save token cost, or to pay more for lower tail latency. Existing docs are qualitative. This initiative builds a small experimental platform and methodology to create defensible, reproducible recommendations for real workloads (RAG, chat, summarization) and to inform optimizer tooling (Redwood Optimize).
objectives: Design 3 canonical synthetic workloads and 2 anonymized customer workloads for lab runs
Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token, and variance for each model variant and quantization level
Characterize tail-latency behavior under realistic batching and autoscale scenarios
Produce a runbook with decision flow and recommended thresholds for model selection by use-case
Surface inputs for Redwood Optimize to calibrate batching/quantization suggestions
success_criteria: Lab runs completed for at least 4 model families (small/medium/large/quantized) across hosted/dedicated setups
Decision runbook drafted and validated with two internal product teams
Three example rule-of-thumb charts (latency vs $/k tokens) published to Console docs
Bench dashboards with reproducible experiment artifacts linked in the runbook
deliverables: experiment harness (Terraform + scripts) that spins up repeatable testbeds
bench dashboard (Grafana link) displaying latency/cost breakdowns
public runbook in Confluence: 'Latency-Cost Tradeoff — Playbook'
internal RFC summarizing recommendations and trade-offs for go-to-market messaging
